## Incident Report: STRRAT RAT Infection — 172.16.1.66

**Evidence reviewed:** `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (11,562 packets, 2024-07-30 06:38:48–06:48:34 UTC, 585.7s). No IDS/Suricata export or other artifacts were present in the evidence directory — findings are derived entirely from packet analysis with `tshark`.

### Victim host
| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **172.16.1.66** | Sole non-infrastructure host generating traffic |
| MAC address | **00:1e:64:ec:f3:08** | ARP / Ethernet source address |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-SKBR25F** | NBNS name registration; AD DNS record `DESKTOP-SKBR25F.wiresharkworkshop.online`; confirmed independently inside the malware's own beacon (below) |
| Domain | wiresharkworkshop.online (DC: WIRESHARK-WS-DC / 172.16.1.4) | LDAP/Kerberos/NBNS traffic |
| Logged-in user | **collier** (as self-reported by the malware) / Kerberos principal **ccollier** | Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString from 172.16.1.66; matches malware beacon field |
| OS | Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit, Windows Defender active | Reported in malware beacon |

### Malware family
**STRRAT** (Java-based RAT), **version 1.6**, campaign/bot ID `1BE8292C`.

**Attribution basis: signature-confirmed**, not behavioral inference. The C2 channel is a raw, unencrypted TCP protocol, and its keep-alive frames contain the malware's own literal self-identification string. Decoded from packet payload (e.g., frame 9119, T+78.07s):

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|collier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender||1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|1 Sec
```

This is STRRAT's documented pipe-delimited ping format: `ping|STRRAT|<botid>|<hostname>|<user>|<os>|<arch>|<AV>|<active_window_b64>|<version>|<country>|<java_installed>|<uptime>`. Later pings (from ~T+575s onward) add a base64 active-window field, e.g. `UHJvZ3JhbSBNYW5hZ2Vy` = `Program Manager`, matching STRRAT's known idle-window-title reporting behavior.

### Timeline
- **T+64.05s–68.06s** — A Java TLS client on 172.16.1.66 (JA3 `026e5ca865ce1f09da3a81d8a4e3effb`, distinct from the host's browser JA3 `65005c9d9ae0f0ebeaf22c210571d482` seen on normal Bing/MSN traffic) connects to `github.com` (140.82.113.3), pulls ~828 KB from `objects.githubusercontent.com` (185.199.110.133), then opens three parallel TLS sessions to `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209/199.232.192.209) transferring ~8.9 MB total — consistent with a Java loader staging its payload/runtime before execution. All three sessions share the same JA3, confirming one process performed the sequence.
- **T+76.99s** — TCP SYN to **141.98.10.79:12132** (C2), no TLS.
- **T+77.96s** — Cleartext HTTP `GET /json/` to `ip-api.com` (208.95.112.1), UA `Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/73.0.3683.86 Safari/537.36`; response confirms self-geolocation (US, Texas, Austin) — classic RAT victim-profiling.
- **T+78.07s onward** — STRRAT `ping` beacons to 141.98.10.79:12132 every ~5 seconds, continuing unbroken through the end of the capture (T+585.66s, still active when the pcap ends).

### Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `141.98.10.79:12132` — TCP, plaintext, STRRAT ping protocol (primary and only observed C2 endpoint/port)

**Domains/services abused for staging and profiling** (legitimate infrastructure abused, not inherently malicious domains, but part of the observed infection chain):
- `github.com` → 140.82.113.3
- `objects.githubusercontent.com` → 185.199.110.133 (also .108/.109/.111.133 in DNS answer)
- `repo1.maven.org` → 199.232.196.209 / 199.232.192.209
- `ip-api.com` → 208.95.112.1 (victim geolocation check, `GET http://ip-api.com/json/`)

**File names / SHA256 hashes:** **None recoverable.** All staging traffic (GitHub / githubusercontent / Maven) was TLS-encrypted, and no TLS key log or other decryption material was included in the evidence set — only SNI, JA3, and byte counts are observable from the capture, so the specific payload filename, path, or hash cannot be extracted from this pcap. The only cleartext HTTP transactions in the capture are the benign NCSI check (`www.msftconnecttest.com/connecttest.txt`) and the `ip-api.com/json/` lookup; neither carries a file transfer.

**No malicious URLs with full paths are visible** for the same reason (TLS). If a keylog file or the endpoint's disk image becomes available, decrypting the 64s–68s TLS sessions to objects.githubusercontent.com/repo1.maven.org would be the next step to recover the actual staged file(s) and compute hashes.

### Summary
172.16.1.66 (DESKTOP-SKBR25F, user collier/ccollier) is infected with **STRRAT v1.6** (bot ID `1BE8292C`), confirmed by the malware's own cleartext C2 protocol strings. The host staged its payload via GitHub/Maven infrastructure using a non-browser Java TLS client, performed an IP geolocation self-check against ip-api.com, and has maintained a persistent 5-second beacon to **141.98.10.79:12132** for the remainder of the capture. Recommend isolating the host immediately, blocking 141.98.10.79/12132 at the perimeter, and resetting the ccollier domain credentials given STRRAT's known credential/browser-password-theft capability.
